title.narrative: Supporting the National Response to HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria in Angola - Angola (01-Jul-2021-30-Jun-2024)

description.narrative: Angola, Multicomponent, United Nations Development Programme (UNDP Angola)This program has the following goals: Reduce new infections, morbidity and mortality from HIV/AIDS by 2024. Decrease TB incidence from 355 to 325 per 100.000 inhabitants by 2023 (355 per 100,000 is the incidence estimated by WHO in 2018). Decrease TB mortality from 7% in 2019 to less than 5% by 2023. Reduce by 40% the morbidity and mortality of malaria in the 4 provinces by 2025 compared to baseline in 2019. The objectives of this program are: Reduce new HIV infections by at least 20% among the general population by 2024.. Reduce new HIV infections among children born to HIV infected mothers by 60% by 2024.. Increasing the coverage of PLHIV on ART from 24 % and 15 % in 2019 to 63% and 60% in adults and children, respectively, by 2024. Develop a favorable ethical and legal enviroment for reduction of stigma and discrimation against people living and affected by HIV, key and vulnerable population.. Increase the number of notified TB cases from 70.362 in 2018 to 101.530 in 2024. Increase the treatment success rate of sensitive TB (all forms) from 25% in 2017 to 85% in 2024. Increase the number of notified MDRTB cases from 1,523 in 2019 to 2,848 in 2024.. By 2024, at least 90% of the population in target provinces uses LLINs as method of malaria prevention. By 2024, 100% of suspected malaria cases at health facility, and community levels are tested before receiving treatment.. By 2024, 100% of malaria cases testing positive are treated according to the national guidelines, at all levels of the national health pyramid, including at community level;. By the end of 2024, 90% of health facilities are reporting their monthly reports.. By the 2024, 90% of health facilities monthly reports are submitted timely.
